skill_snapshot_hash_method: SHA-256 of sorted relative-path sha256sum lines for every file under skills/cdm-dev
production_tree_hash_method: SHA-256 of each sorted repository-relative src/main path, a NUL separator, and that file's SHA-256 digest followed by a newline
note: Four counted, sequential, context-isolated arms used Claude Code 2.1.227 with claude-sonnet-5 or Codex CLI 0.147.0 with gpt-5.4, all at high effort and authenticated through local Claude Max or ChatGPT subscriptions with API credential/provider overrides removed. Each received the identical checksummed open-design task and pinned CDM 7.0.0 artifacts; controls could not read cdm-dev, this repository, the rubric, evaluator probes, or sibling workspaces. Every candidate was committed before evaluator tests were adapted to its public API. Claude Fable 5 independently rebuilt and inspected all four, executed generated child validators, ran the fixed probes, and scored Sonnet treatment/control 99/94 and GPT-5.4 treatment/control 87/93. The skill gave Sonnet a materially better CDM graph and validator boundary but cost 30 percent more wall time; GPT treatment was cheaper than its control but introduced a skipped-date fail-window bug. The bounded query ceiling, simple-name API lookup, complete-boundary floor, populated-child validation recipe, dated policy-window rule, monetary-scale assertion, and repo remedy-scope guidance added after the run are not credited to treatment.

independent_review.leakage_verdict: no content leakage; one shared Gradle daemon exposed sibling path names only after design completion
findings: All four arms pass the public economic, direction, scope-isolation, identity, and deterministic-state probes with exact decimal arithmetic.
Sonnet treatment is the only implementation whose terminated TradeState, populated children, and emitted CDM Money all pass the generated validator sweep.
Sonnet control omits required ClosedState.activityDate and its root-only validation never runs ClosedStateValidator.
GPT treatment models a dated fail window as a current-call flag, so a skipped failed day is accrued unfloored when the landing date resolves the fail.
Both GPT boundaries contain incomplete generated Trade graphs; treatment's identity shell fails TradeValidator and control's empty populated children fail their own validators.
The skill improves Sonnet correctness by five points but makes GPT-5.4 six points worse despite reducing that arm's input tokens and commands.

negative_rate_window_and_resumption.gpt-5.4-with-skill: public sequence passes; skipped-date resolution probe fails with EUR 277.78 paid to failing seller

offer_side_and_bid_invariance.gpt-5.4-with-skill: start-leg public path passes; quote-derived end-leg path selects bid

generated_boundary_validator_sweep.gpt-5.4-with-skill: fail: Trade product, tradeLot, counterparty, and tradeDate absent; ClosedState passes
generated_boundary_validator_sweep.gpt-5.4-control: fail: populated product and counterparties fail their own validators; ClosedState passes

skill_revision_after_run.change: Made source and API lookup batched and package-safe; imposed a compiler-driven helper-call ceiling; distinguished complete boundaries from labelled partial fixtures and prohibited hollow child shells; added a mechanical populated-child validator walk, fail-loud dependency-injection guidance, dated windowed-policy state, monetary minor-unit assertions, and transaction-remedy scope guidance.
skill_revision_after_run.credit: not credited to any recorded treatment arm

harness_limitations: One GPT treatment Gradle --info output listed sibling workspace path names through a long-lived shared daemon; sandbox logs show no sibling file access and the design predated that output.
Future arms must use a per-arm GRADLE_USER_HOME and --no-daemon or stop daemons between arms.
Cross-vendor token and cost values are not comparable; comparisons are made only within model/vendor pairs.
